metadata.technology_specification: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) system
metadata.technology_reasoning: Triple Quadrupole LC–MS/MS systems are the industry standard for targeted quantitative analysis in life sciences, environmental and food safety testing due to their high sensitivity and selectivity. As of 2024, these systems dominate the mass spectrometry market segment for routine and regulatory applications due to their robust triple quadrupole mass analyzers and integration with liquid chromatography for sample separation.

components.reasoning: Essential for sample separation before mass analysis; procured as a modular unit with pumps, injector, and column compartment.
Core mass spectrometry component comprising three quadrupoles for precursor selection, fragmentation, and product ion filtering; always a separate major subassembly.
Electrospray Ionization (ESI) or Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionization (APCI) source generates ions from the LC effluent; a distinct and critical module.
High-vacuum pumps (turbomolecular and roughing pumps) maintain the ultra-high vacuum needed inside the mass analyzer; critical and procured separately.
Electron multiplier or similar device that detects ions exiting the quadrupoles; a key functional subassembly.
Computing hardware and software used for instrument control, data acquisition, and processing; usually a separate subsystem.
Collision cell between Q1 and Q3 for ion fragmentation, often considered distinct within the triple quadrupole assembly but sometimes modularized separately.
Includes autosampler or manual injection system delivering samples to LC; a distinct component from LC pumps and columns.
Structural housing that supports and protects components, designed to isolate vibration and electromagnetic interference, standard in all systems.

Liquid Chromatography System (LC).name: C18 silica
Liquid Chromatography System (LC).reasoning: Primary stationary phase material for chromatographic separation, universally used in LC columns for retention of analytes, critical for the system's function.

Liquid Chromatography System (LC).name: Stainless steel
Liquid Chromatography System (LC).reasoning: Common material for tubing and fittings due to chemical resistance and strength, industry standard in LC hardware construction.

Liquid Chromatography System (LC).name: Glass
Liquid Chromatography System (LC).reasoning: Used in solvent reservoirs and sometimes in flow cells for optical detection, transparent and chemically inert, widely used though some plastics can substitute.

Liquid Chromatography System (LC).name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Liquid Chromatography System (LC).reasoning: Used in tubing and bottles for solvent storage and waste collection, common polymer with good chemical resistance; alternative polymers exist but PET is widely used.

Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.name: Stainless steel
Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.reasoning: Primary structural and electrode material for quadrupole rods and vacuum chambers due to strength, conductivity and vacuum compatibility; industry standard.

Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.name: Copper
Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.reasoning: Used for electrical connections and wiring within the analyzer, excellent conductivity and standard in electronics and vacuum systems.

Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.name: Ceramic
Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.reasoning: Used as insulators and supports for quadrupole rods due to good electrical insulation and thermal stability, common though some specific advanced ceramics vary.

Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.name: Aluminum
Triple Quadrupole Mass Analyzer.reasoning: Used in some structural parts and heat sinks; alternatives like stainless steel exist but aluminum is common for lightweight components.

Ion Source.name: Tungsten
Ion Source.reasoning: Widely used filament material in electron ionization sources due to high melting point and stability; critical for ion generation.

Ion Source.name: Stainless steel
Ion Source.reasoning: Structural components and vacuum-compatible parts; standard and reliable material in ion source construction.

Ion Source.name: Copper
Ion Source.reasoning: Used for electrical contacts and heat dissipation parts, common but some alternatives exist.

Ion Source.name: Ceramic
Ion Source.reasoning: Insulation and mounting components to electrically isolate parts; ceramics are common but alternatives available.

Vacuum System.name: Stainless steel
Vacuum System.reasoning: Primary material for vacuum chambers and piping due to excellent vacuum integrity, corrosion resistance, and mechanical strength; essential and industry standard.

Vacuum System.name: Copper
Vacuum System.reasoning: Utilized in seals (copper gaskets) and electrical wiring in pumps and instrumentation; standard material in vacuum technology.

Vacuum System.name: Vacuum pump materials
Vacuum System.reasoning: Specialized materials designed for pump internals to maintain vacuum performance; essential for vacuum pump function.

Detector.name: Photomultiplier tube materials
Detector.reasoning: Critical for signal amplification in common MS detectors, specialized glass and photocathode materials required; essential for detector function.

Detector.name: Borosilicate glass
Detector.reasoning: Used for optical windows and detector housing, chemical stability and optical clarity are key; standard material.

Detector.name: Silver
Detector.reasoning: Used in electrical contacts and conductive coatings within the detector; standard though sometimes substituted by other conductors.

Data System and Control Electronics.name: Silicon
Data System and Control Electronics.reasoning: Fundamental semiconductor material for integrated circuits and microprocessors controlling the system; absolutely essential.

Data System and Control Electronics.name: Copper
Data System and Control Electronics.reasoning: Used in printed circuit board traces and wiring for electrical conductivity; very standard and critical.

Data System and Control Electronics.name: Aluminum
Data System and Control Electronics.reasoning: Employed in heat sinks and some connector housings for thermal management; alternatives exist but commonly used.

Data System and Control Electronics.name: Epoxy resins
Data System and Control Electronics.reasoning: Used as insulating adhesives and encapsulants in electronics; standard practice but some alternatives present.

Interface/Collision Cell.name: Stainless steel
Interface/Collision Cell.reasoning: Primary structural and chamber materials for collision cells and interfaces due to corrosion resistance and vacuum compatibility; industry standard.

Interface/Collision Cell.name: Copper
Interface/Collision Cell.reasoning: Used for electrical connections and heat dissipation; common and necessary for cell operation.

Interface/Collision Cell.name: Ceramic
Interface/Collision Cell.reasoning: For electrical insulation and component support inside the collision cell, commonly used but alternatives exist.

Sample Introduction System.name: Stainless steel
Sample Introduction System.reasoning: Used for needles, tubing, and other flow paths requiring high purity, corrosion resistance, and mechanical strength; standard industry material.

Sample Introduction System.name: Glass
Sample Introduction System.reasoning: Used in sample vials, capillaries, and inserts for chemical inertness and transparency, common though plastic alternatives exist.

Sample Introduction System.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Sample Introduction System.reasoning: Material for some tubing and sample containers, used for chemical resistance though alternatives are available.

Chassis/Enclosure.name: Aluminum
Chassis/Enclosure.reasoning: Primary material for lightweight, corrosion-resistant chassis and enclosures; widely used for thermal management and structural support.

Chassis/Enclosure.name: Steel Ingots
Chassis/Enclosure.reasoning: Used in frames and reinforcements, strong and cost-effective; common but alternatives like aluminum exist.

Chassis/Enclosure.name: Epoxy resins
Chassis/Enclosure.reasoning: Used for coatings and insulating parts inside the enclosure; alternatives exist but epoxy resins are standard for insulation and protective coatings.
